h1: The 7 Best File Drawers Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best File Drawers Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 file drawers and cabinets under $100 scored on build, locks, wheels, paper size and assembly.
summary: The Approgreent 2 Drawer Metal File Cabinet is the best file drawer under $100, a fully assembled steel unit with an anti-tipping design and a lock. The fully assembled 3-drawer mobile cabinet is the pick for more capacity. The Sbanmao fits letter and legal files on locking wheels, and the SISESOL is the budget unit with full-extension drawers.
intro: The cheapest way to ruin a file cabinet is to load the top drawer first. A two- or three-drawer unit with all the weight up high tips forward the moment you open it, and the cheap ones do not have an interlock. That single design flaw explains more broken cabinets than any lock or slide.

So this ranking starts with stability, then moves to the practical details: whether the drawers hold letter and legal folders, whether the lock is real, whether the wheels lock, and whether you have to build it yourself. We reviewed seven file cabinets that all stay under $100, and scored them on the Primea framework with build quality and everyday usability weighted most.

products.name: Approgreent 2 Drawer Metal File Cabinet
products.verdict: A fully assembled steel two-drawer cabinet with smooth wheels, a lock and an anti-tipping design.
products.description:
The Approgreent is a fully assembled steel filing cabinet with two drawers, smooth mobility, secure locking and an anti-tipping design. Anti-tipping matters more than any other spec on a file cabinet: it stops a second drawer from opening while the first is out, which is the cause of most tipping accidents.

It wins because steel and assembly combine in one listing. The plastic mobile cabinets cost less to ship but flex under a full load of paper, and a cabinet that arrives built skips the hour of screws that wrecks many budget units. The $50 to $100 band is the same as the other leading picks, but only two drawers limits capacity.

Buy it for a home office with a moderate filing load. Skip it if you need three drawers.
products.idealFor: Home offices with a moderate paper load who want it built and stable.
products.skipIf: You need three drawers of capacity.

products.name: Fully Assembled 3-Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock
products.verdict: Three drawers that fit common file sizes, fully assembled, mobile and lockable.
products.description:
This mobile cabinet gives you three drawers, flexible organization, a fit for common file sizes and secure personal storage with a lock. It also arrives fully assembled, which for a three-drawer unit saves a long, awkward build.

It ranks second because the Approgreent states steel and an anti-tipping design, while this listing does not describe the frame material or tip protection. Three drawers help you split active, archive and supplies, and the extra capacity is the reason to pick it. The $50 to $100 band is the same.

Good for anyone who needs to separate paperwork into categories under one lock. Check whether the full listing mentions anti-tip protection before loading the top drawer.
products.idealFor: People sorting active files, archives and supplies in one cabinet.
products.skipIf: You want a documented steel build.

products.name: Sbanmao Letter/Legal Rolling File Cabinet
products.verdict: A rolling cabinet that states letter and legal file support, on 360 degree lockable wheels.
products.description:
The Sbanmao is the one cabinet that states letter and legal compatibility in its name, and it rolls on 360 degree lockable wheels. Legal support is rarer than it sounds: many budget drawers are cut for letter folders only, and legal documents curl over the edge or do not fit.

It ranks third because the listing does not mention drawers count, steel or anti-tip design, so it offers less assurance on build than the two above. In exchange, you get the clearest paper-size claim and a price of $25 to $50. The lockable casters mean it stays put while you pull a drawer.

A smart pick for a home office dealing with contracts and legal-size paper. Check the drawer count on the full page.
products.idealFor: Home offices with legal-size contracts and forms.
products.skipIf: You need a documented steel frame.

products.name: SISESOL 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock and Wheels
products.verdict: A two-drawer cabinet with a lock, wheels and full-extension drawers in the $25 to $50 band.
products.description:
SISESOL's two-drawer cabinet lists secure storage, full extension and a mobile design with a lock and wheels. Full extension lets the drawer slide completely out, so you can reach the folder at the back without twisting. On a cabinet this cheap, it is not a given.

It ranks fourth because the Approgreent and the fully assembled three-drawer unit state assembly and construction details, while this one does not. In its favor, it costs $25 to $50, about half the price of the top picks, and still gives the three features that matter most: full extension, a lock and wheels. Assembly is likely a task, so budget time.

Buy it as a value file cabinet for a desk-side corner. Skip it if you need steel or anti-tip details.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want full-extension drawers and a lock.
products.skipIf: You want a documented steel frame.

products.name: TEEALUBAN 3 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock
products.verdict: A compact three-drawer unit with less assembly and separate zones for files and supplies.
products.description:
The TEEALUBAN is a three-drawer file cabinet with a lock, pitched as needing less assembly and keeping files and supplies separate. It is built as compact desk-side storage, so it tucks beside a desk rather than standing as a free-floating unit.

It ranks fifth because the listing is mostly style-oriented and does not give materials, wheel details or the exact drawer layout. The separate zones for files and supplies are a useful feature in practice, since a mixed drawer of folders and pens turns into a mess. It sits in the $50 to $100 band alongside the leaders.

A solid fit for a small home office that wants compact storage. Verify the dimensions against your desk.
pros: Three drawers in a compact body
products.idealFor: Small home offices needing compact desk-side storage.
products.skipIf: You want wheels and a documented steel build.

products.name: Guizeeopo Filing Cabinets for Home Office
products.verdict: A home office filing cabinet with ample storage, easy mobility, secure locking and a stable design.
products.description:
The Guizeeopo is pitched at the home office with ample storage space, easy mobility, secure locking and a stable, secure design. Those are the right four boxes to tick, but the listing offers little to verify them: no drawer count, no material, no paper size.

It ranks sixth because the leaders back similar claims with specifics such as steel, full extension or letter and legal support. At $50 to $100 it asks the same price as the top two. The stable design wording hints at some anti-tip thinking, but without a named mechanism, treat it with caution and avoid overloading the top drawer.

A decent fit if you find it at a discount. Read the full listing for drawer count and size first.
products.idealFor: Home offices where a mobile locked cabinet fits the space.
products.skipIf: You want specifics on drawers, steel and paper size.

products.name: VASAGLE 2-Drawer File Cabinet
products.verdict: A modern two-drawer cabinet that blends into a room and works as an all-round storage unit.
products.description:
VASAGLE's two-drawer file cabinet leans on design: it promises simple modern looks for seamless room integration, an efficient file-storage solution and a space-saving, multi-purpose design. It is the cabinet you can put in a living room without it looking like an office.

It ranks last because the emphasis is on style, and the listing gives no lock, wheel or steel claim. The lock is the main gap, since the other six units secure papers and this one does not mention it. At $25 to $50 it is cheap, and the multi-purpose angle suits a cabinet holding both files and household items.

A good pick for shared living spaces. Skip it if you need to lock sensitive documents.
products.idealFor: Shared rooms that need discreet file storage.
products.skipIf: You need to lock sensitive documents.

whatMatters.detail: A file cabinet tips when more than one drawer is open at once, because the weight moves forward. Anti-tipping designs lock the other drawers or widen the base. Look for the phrase on the listing, as with the Approgreent, and always load the bottom drawer with the heaviest folders.

Steel resists flexing and holds a full load of paper without bowing, while plastic or thin board can warp over time. Look for steel or metal in the title or specs. A cabinet with no material listed deserves caution, and a visit to the full product page before you buy.

Letter folders fit nearly every drawer, but legal folders need a wider and deeper box. The Sbanmao states letter and legal compatibility. Check the interior width in inches if listed, and confirm what you file before choosing, because a legal folder that curls will jam the slide.

A lock protects sensitive papers from visitors, and lockable wheels keep a mobile unit from rolling away as you pull a drawer. Lower-priced locks deter casual access but are not secure. Check that the listing mentions both, and keep truly sensitive documents in a proper safe.

A fully assembled cabinet arrives ready to load, while flat-pack units can take an hour or more. Loose screws are a common failure point on self-assembled cabinets. Look for fully assembled in the title, as on the Approgreent, and budget time and a second person if it is not.

faq.q: Do these file drawers fit hanging folders?
faq.a: Many do, but check each listing. The Fully Assembled 3-Drawer cabinet states it fits common file sizes, and the Sbanmao lists letter and legal. Measure your folders and the drawer interior before buying, especially for legal-size hanging folders.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake loading a file cabinet?
faq.a: Filling the top drawer first. Weight high up makes the cabinet front-heavy, and opening two drawers at once can tip it. Put heavy folders in the bottom drawer of the Approgreent or SISESOL and keep the top light.

faq.q: Is the steel Approgreent worth it over the SISESOL?
faq.a: If you file heavily, yes. The Approgreent is steel, fully assembled and anti-tipping. The SISESOL costs $25 to $50 and adds full-extension slides, which suits lighter use and tight budgets.

faq.q: How do I assemble and place a file cabinet?
faq.a: Choose a level floor, lock the wheels on mobile units such as the Sbanmao, and load the bottom drawer first. Fully assembled models like the Approgreent save the build, and flat-pack ones take about an hour.

faq.q: How do I maintain the slides and lock?
faq.a: Wipe the tracks and add a light dry lubricant if they stick, and keep a spare key away from the cabinet. Check wheel locks periodically on the SISESOL and Guizeeopo, since dust can stop them seating.

faq.q: Can these cabinets hold sensitive documents?
faq.a: A cabinet lock deters casual access but is not high security. The Approgreent and TEEALUBAN include locks, and the VASAGLE lists none. For passports and deeds, use a fireproof safe instead.

finalTake: The Approgreent 2 Drawer Metal File Cabinet is the best file drawer under $100, thanks to a steel body, an anti-tipping design and a fully assembled build. The fully assembled 3-drawer cabinet is the choice for more capacity, and the Sbanmao is right for legal-size paper. Load the bottom drawer first on any of them, and treat the lock as a deterrent, not a vault.
